Le Mondial de l'automobile de Paris témo: The Paris Motor Show demonstrates a clear resurgence in vitality for the industry, refuting the pessimistic predictions made in the wake of the health crisis. While the gradual disappearance of major industry gatherings was feared, this edition confirms the recovery of activities. Some sixty manufacturers answered the call to exhibit their concepts and new products, despite the notable absence of luxury brands.
La confrontation commerciale se traduit: The commercial competition is visibly reflected in the occupancy of exhibition spaces. While Renault retains the event's largest stand, Chinese groups show a strengthened presence with around twenty brands mobilized. Among the latter, Chery and AITO rank second and third in surface area, ahead of traditional players like Peugeot, Volkswagen, and Mercedes. Other manufacturers, such as Smart, relied on the visual originality of their installations to generate interest.
Dès l'ouverture au public le mardi 13 oc: From the opening to the public on Tuesday, October 13, steady crowds were observed in the aisles, notably around the 2 CV at Citroën. Sales teams multiplied contacts with visitors. Although the Paris Automotive Summit, held on the same date, recalled the persistence of economic and political challenges, industry leaders hold a less alarmist tone. Finally, users' perception of electric technology is evolving favorably, illustrating a clear decline in prejudices compared to previous years.
